findings.text: declared_backend_search_path() resolves the flight layers with flight.resolve() and no project, so a backends.<name>.search_path declared in a project's own layer (docs/state/<project>/flight.yaml) is never read; the feature silently misses exactly the layer whose backends this deployment declares, and preflight_launch_command and assert_routable_backends_resolvable both already hold the project-resolved backend mapping and discard it

reckon/crew/dispatch.py calls _persisted_worker_environment({}, facts=dispatch_host) without backend_name, so the persisted directive PATH omits the declared backend directories while _supervisor_spec's launch PATH now carries them; the two records of one dispatch disagree and the file is outside this node's write paths

The committed evidence fragment's gate table cites logs/head-importers.log (the uncommitted-worktree arm, whose 15 ids are identical to the base) and states 'zero added ids', but the arm at the landed revision is logs/head-importers-at-600cba4d68.log, which has one added id and two removed; the landed evidence claims a result the landed arm contradicts

flight.py's availability report still locates a backend command with bare shutil.which(command) against the process PATH, so a backend resolvable only through the newly declared search_path reports command_found false and detail "'<command>' is not on PATH" while a launch now resolves it; the change makes the two views of the same backend disagree
